name: AI and Faith homepage: interfaith network on AI ethics
title: AI and Faith homepage: interfaith network on AI ethics
answer: This is the homepage of AI and Faith, a global interfaith network of faith leaders, scholars, technologists, ethicists, educators and partner organisations. Its most useful statement is that the world's religions offer ancient wisdom that should guide AI development and use, and that AI ethics is both deeply moral and, for the 85 percent of people who claim a religious affiliation, deeply spiritual. It is a mission and signup page, not a detailed programme report.

sections.body: AI and Faith publishes this page as its homepage. The text presents AI and Faith as a global network of faith leaders and communities, scholars, technologists, ethicists, educators and partner organisations. It is a mission and engagement page rather than a research paper or report. Its scope is the ethical and moral issues around artificial intelligence and related technologies, framed through the wisdom of the world's religious traditions. No publication date is stated. The page includes calls to donate and to sign up for a monthly newsletter.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: AI and Faith says it works for a future in which artificial intelligence serves humankind under five strategic pillars. It argues that the issues raised by AI are at root deeply moral, and that for the 85 percent of the world's population who claim a religious affiliation they are deeply spiritual as well. The organisation believes the world's religions offer ancient wisdom that should guide the development and use of AI technology in contemporary society. It says it encourages, connects and equips tech creators, academic researchers, ethicists, theologians and other related professionals to engage the world in the moral and ethical issues around AI and related technologies. It wants to shape the discussion in deeply thoughtful and life affirming ways. Its stated focus is to bring the fundamental values of the world's major religions into the emerging debate on the ethical development of AI and related technologies. It seeks to apply values important in the world of faith to essential questions emerging from new forms of intelligence. The page includes a quotation saying the goal of AI and Faith is to inject humility and historicity into an industry that has often rejected them both, and to bring faith based, literary, classical and oral traditions to bear on what may be the most important technological transformation of our time. AI and Faith describes itself as a pluralist organisation seeking to engage the world in these moral and ethical issues.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that 85 percent of the world's population claim a religious affiliation. It states that AI and Faith works under five strategic pillars, but it does not list or name those pillars. It describes AI and Faith as a global network and a pluralist organisation. It includes a quotation, without attribution in the text, that the goal of AI and Faith is to inject humility and historicity into an industry that has often rejected them both. It also says the organisation offers a monthly newsletter and accepts tax deductible gifts. No other specific numbers or definitions are given.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Churches and Faith Organisations can use this source to identify AI and Faith as an interfaith network that connects faith leaders, scholars, technologists, ethicists, educators and partner organisations around AI ethics. It supports the industry page point that AI and Faith convenes ethics work, though the page itself uses the language of encouraging, connecting and equipping rather than convening. It is useful for understanding how a faith based organisation frames AI as a moral and spiritual issue and argues that religious traditions should inform AI development. It does not provide practical guidance, case studies or programme details for churches or faith organisations.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Churches and Faith Organisations

sections.body: This is a homepage with mission level content. It does not cover specific projects, events, publications, named leaders, membership details or the five strategic pillars it mentions. It gives no publication date and no geographic detail beyond global. It is partly promotional, asking for donations and newsletter signups. The harvested text also includes an unrelated Italian passage about game design and mobile access, which appears to be scraping noise rather than part of the organisation's message. The page is therefore useful as a statement of positioning, not as a detailed source on AI deployment in religious contexts.
